scope: Queueing, inventory control, and spatial matching follow-up. This supplements the earlier November 9 audits and is not a complete reassessment of the catalogue.
method: Read primary-source models and relevant theorem statements, inspect version and publication metadata, compare assumptions and benchmarks, and search for follow-up work. Record abstract-only leads separately. A theorem-statement check is not independent proof certification.
limitations: Only eight existing entries received substantive theorem/model updates. The other selected entries were triaged, not recertified; unsuccessful searches do not establish open status.
No complete manuscript proof was independently verified. Preprint results are attributed claims, not referee-certified conclusions.

Bu, Gong, and Yin (Management Science, online August 26, 2026) was checked through publisher metadata and its abstract. Its full theorem assumptions were inaccessible, so the record does not assert a theorem for the catalogue's baseline from that abstract.
The skill-based routing question is an editorially extracted bound gap, not a quoted author conjecture. The lower-bound comparison requires admissible reward alternatives.

The finite inventory counterexample is reproduced for integer orders at seven selected initial states, with exact arithmetic and all reachable states. This is not a verification of every result in the paper.
No git push or live deployment is part of this pass.

entries.summary: The general-service saturated stochastic recurrence gives a stability-threshold representation. Reframed the residual question as certified efficient evaluation of its growth constant, not existence of a threshold. Numerical agreement of lower estimates is not a certified error bound; critical-load behavior is separate.

Added the residual-service mean bound while retaining Assumptions 1-3, including non-lattice service and the auxiliary-queue recurrence/convergence assumption. Distinguished waiting jobs from jobs in service and mean bounds from exact stationary laws. Corrected Takayuki Osogami's name and replaced vague/Wikipedia references with paper citations.

entries.summary: Specified the Schur-complement reflection matrix and tightness equations. Distinguished uniform integrability of unscaled high-priority queues from weaker scaled SSC. Added two-station classification and LBFS cases. The non-tight three-station example does not refute tightness implying stability/SSC.

entries.summary: Replaced the already answered generic asymptotic-optimality question with finite-parameter guarantees for a fixed zero-lead-time FIFO model. Included the 2024 large-penalty results, distinguishing sublinear mean excess, regularly varying tails, and bounded-demand exact optimality. Marked the 2026 positive-lead-time article as related abstract-only evidence.

entries.summary: Corrected the model to finite-horizon, nonstationary demand, zero lead time and complete backordering. The counterexample is not a stationary infinite-horizon lost-sales result. Reframed the surviving question as complexity of exact ordering-region structure.

entries.summary: Retained the previously recorded 2026 approximation progress, qualified PIL demand assumptions, and separated large-penalty and large-lead-time regimes. Added the explicit fixed-lead-time regularly varying tail question: the available ratio bound does not establish ratio one. Prior-pass 2026 claims are retained, not independently re-proved here.

entries.summary: Removed the balanced one-dimensional iid batch case from the open target: greedy is constant-competitive there. Corrected fully dynamic replenishment (demand does not wait). Kept higher-dimensional and replenishing-market greedy questions; SOAR's separate semi-dynamic exponent result is not a theorem for ordinary greedy.

entries.summary: Added the instance-dependent logarithmic versus polylogarithmic regret gap for skill-based queue routing. Retained fixed positive slack, completion feedback, stability, consistency and nondegeneracy. Bernoulli lower bounds require confusing alternatives inside the admissible family. This is an extracted gap, not a quoted conjecture; confidence is medium.
